hints: Look carefully at compound Z and list every acidic group it contains, carboxylic acid, alcohol and ester.
Remember that sodium carbonate is a mild base, strong enough to deprotonate carboxylic acids but not ordinary alcohols.
Check whether cold, dilute carbonate can hydrolyse an ester, then decide which group is the only one to change.
walkthrough:
**Identify the functional groups in Z**

Compound Z contains three types of oxygen groups. There is one carboxylic acid, $\text{CO}_2\text{H}$, three alcohol $\text{OH}$ groups on the ring, and one ester $\text{RCOOR'}$ on the right side.

Think of it as: $\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ + $3 \times \text{ROH}$ + $1 \times$ ester

**Compare acid strengths**

Carboxylic acids are much stronger acids than alcohols. Sodium carbonate solution will neutralise acids to release $\text{CO}_2$:
$$\text{RCO}_2\text{H} + \text{CO}_3^{2-} \rightarrow \text{RCO}_2^- + \text{HCO}_3^-$$
Alcohols with $pK_a$ around 16 to 18 are far weaker than carbonic acid, so $\text{ROH} + \text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$ shows no reaction at room temperature.

**Rule out ester hydrolysis**

Ester hydrolysis to a carboxylate and an alcohol needs strong alkali like $\text{NaOH}$ with heating. Cold, dilute $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$ solution does not hydrolyse the ester in good yield.

So only one change happens: $\text{CO}_2\text{H} \rightarrow \text{CO}_2\text{Na}$, while all $\text{OH}$ groups and the ester stay unchanged.

options.A: Correct. Only the carboxylic acid reacts with excess sodium carbonate to form the sodium carboxylate, $\text{CO}_2\text{Na}$. The three alcohol groups are too weakly acidic to react, and the ester is untouched under these mild, room temperature conditions.
options.B: Incorrect. This shows the carboxylic acid plus all three alcohols converted to $\text{ONa}$ salts. Students choosing this forget that ordinary alcohols do not react with sodium carbonate, only phenols (partially) and carboxylic acids do.
options.C: Incorrect. This leaves the $\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ unchanged while converting all alcohols to $\text{ONa}$. This is backwards, as the carboxylic acid is the most acidic group and the first to react, while alcohols will not react at all.
options.D: Incorrect. This shows alkaline hydrolysis of the ester to give a triol plus butenoic acid. Ester hydrolysis needs hot concentrated $\text{NaOH}$, not cold dilute $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$, so no cleavage occurs in good yield here.
